A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a poloidal magnetic field can explain the observed rotational evolution in main-sequence stars.
the poloidal field is an essential ingredient for the angular momentum transport, and it is crucial to have a quadrupolar geometry for fast rotators and a dipolar geometry for slow rotators.

the coupling time scale between the radiative core and convective envelope in a 1 M⊙ main sequence star, with a dipolar geometry of the magnetic field, would be 1.2×1010 yr, while the coupling time scale would be 1×107 yr for a quadrupolar geometry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the angular momentum transport by the magnetic field in radiative interiors is strongly dependent on the geometry of the field and the viscosity, but not on the intensity of the field.
the coupling time-scale depends on both viscosity and the geometry and intensity of the magnetic field.
